title: Task Interruption & Resumption
summary: Pause a durable execution at a defined boundary and resume it with validated input, current authority, and reconciled external effects.
overview: Interruption and resumption allow an agent run to wait for a person, missing evidence, a business event, or an operational repair without occupying a worker indefinitely. A durable interrupt records why the run stopped, what input can resume it, and which execution version is waiting. Suspension is a workflow state, not a blocked thread.

Resumption must account for time. Permissions may expire, records may change, and a pending tool call may finish while the run is paused. Validate the resume token and new input, reload current policy, and reconcile outstanding operations before continuing. Do not assume that replaying a paused node is side-effect free.

production.poc: A prototype can pause before a read-only step and manually supply a resume value. Test what code executes again when the runtime restarts that boundary.
production.production: Production persists interrupt metadata, authenticates responders, and defines expiry, cancellation, and stale-input behavior. Place irreversible actions after validated resume boundaries or protect them with idempotency.
production.scale: At scale, waiting runs should consume storage rather than active worker slots. Build queues for expired interrupts and maintain compatibility for executions paused across several deployments.

components.name: Interrupt controller
components.role: Creates a durable waiting state with reason, required input, deadline, and execution version.

components.name: Checkpoint store
components.role: Saves accepted progress and pending operation identities at the suspension boundary.

components.name: Resume gateway
components.role: Authenticates the responder and validates resume identity, input schema, and authority.

components.name: Reconciliation service
components.role: Checks changed business records and uncertain external operations before continuation.

components.name: Expiry scheduler
components.role: Cancels or escalates abandoned waits according to explicit business policy.

flow.title: Reach safe boundary
flow.description: Complete or checkpoint preceding work and identify any outstanding side effects.

flow.title: Persist interrupt
flow.description: Record the expected resume input and state version before releasing the worker.

flow.title: Notify owner
flow.description: Expose the pending action through a durable work queue or authenticated interface.

flow.title: Validate response
flow.description: Reject stale, duplicate, unauthorized, or malformed resume attempts.

flow.title: Refresh assumptions
flow.description: Recheck permissions, source versions, deadlines, and previously uncertain tool outcomes.

flow.title: Continue execution
flow.description: Claim fresh ownership and resume from the documented replay boundary with the accepted input.

diagrams.title: Durable pause and validated continuation
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant W as Agent worker
 participant C as Checkpoint store
 participant H as Review queue
 participant G as Resume gateway
 participant R as Replacement worker
 W->>C: Persist waiting state and resume contract
 W->>H: Publish review task
 H->>G: Authorized decision with state version
 G->>C: Validate and commit resume input
 G->>R: Schedule continuation
 R->>C: Load checkpoint and pending operations
 R->>R: Refresh policy and reconcile effects
 R->>C: Commit next execution state
diagrams.caption: The waiting execution holds no worker, and the responder cannot resume an arbitrary or stale state.

useCase.title: Pausing a purchase request for engineering evidence
useCase.situation: A construction procurement team requests specialized equipment, but engineering certification arrives after the initial assessment.
useCase.problem: Keeping the agent session open wastes capacity, while restarting from scratch repeats supplier checks and loses review context.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must pause with a precise evidence request and resume when the authorized engineer supplies the certificate.
useCase.architecture: A durable interrupt stores the missing certification requirement, approved supplier evidence, and the current purchase-request version.
runtime: The agent finishes available checks and publishes an engineering task with a resume identifier.
On submission, the gateway verifies the engineer's authority, validates the certificate, and confirms that equipment specifications have not changed.
useCase.failure: If the purchase request changed during the wait, the old resume input is retained as evidence but affected checks run again before approval.
useCase.impact: Measure waiting age, stale-resume rejection, resumed-run success, and repeated work to distinguish business delay from runtime inefficiency.

tradeoffs.benefit: Long waits do not occupy scarce worker capacity.
tradeoffs.cost: Checkpoint retention and lifecycle tooling become necessary.

tradeoffs.benefit: Resumption respects changed authority and business facts.
tradeoffs.cost: Some earlier work must be repeated after long pauses.
Code before the interrupt may execute again and needs careful side-effect handling.

failures.scenario: A reviewer submits the same decision twice
failures.detection: Resume gateway finds the state version already advanced.
failures.recovery: Return the recorded outcome without scheduling another continuation.

failures.scenario: A paused execution outlives its workflow version
failures.detection: Loader cannot interpret the old interrupt contract.
failures.recovery: Use a compatible worker or an explicit migration path.

mistakes.fix: Persist operation identity and reconcile the outcome before suspension.

mistakes.mistake: Trusting any bearer of a resume link
mistakes.fix: Authenticate the actor and recheck decision authority.
Persist every value required for continuation.

whenToUse: Tasks wait for people or external evidence.
Long pauses should survive process replacement.
Resume input can be validated against a defined contract.
whenNotToUse: The task can complete within one short stateless request.
Continuation would rely on unrecoverable process-local resources.
No owner or expiry policy exists for waiting work.
checklist: Persist interrupt reason and expected input.
